Tip1: Right-click a column header to sort its tickets. By title, priority, assignee or date. The choice is shared with the project board.
Tip2: Drag a ticket onto another one to turn it into a sub-ticket. The 📂 badge on the parent opens its own sub-kanban.
Tip3: Ctrl+Z undoes your last board actions. Moves, deletes, renames, priority changes. Up to 30 steps back.
Tip4: The search understands tokens. Try #42, @assignee, priority:critical, label:bug or by:owner.
Tip5: Schedule a ticket with ⏰. It will move to its target column by itself when the time comes.
Tip6: The home has two views, each with its own URL. The unified kanban lives at / and the project cards at /projects. Bookmark the one you prefer.
Tip7: Automations can call external services. The httpRequest action fills {ticketId}, {ticketTitle} or {now} for you.
Tip8: Chat with a ticket's assigned agent from its panel. The 💬 button keeps the ticket as context.
Tip9: KittyClaw has no authentication. Its agents run code on this machine. Keep it on localhost, with no tunnel or reverse proxy.
Tip10: Pause a project with ⏸ to stop its automations. Paused projects sink to the bottom of the home, collapsed.
Tip11: Paste an image straight into a description or a comment. It is uploaded and linked automatically.
Tip12: Write #42 in a comment to link a ticket. With #project-slug:7 the reference crosses projects.
Tip13: Everything the UI does is scriptable. The REST API is documented live at /api/docs.
Tip14: Esc closes overlays one at a time. Menu first, then editor, then panel. No mouse needed.
